## Lead qualification workflow, step by step

1. Attract a prospective buyer: Give first-time buyers a reason to start. The homepage, city pages, the free guide and Instagram all point to one value-first offer: a free, personal Buyer Blueprint. Tools: Website builder, Canva, Instagram, Facebook. Benefit: One clear offer across every channel turns passive visitors into people who want to take part. No hard sell is needed to get them started.
2. Capture preferences and requirements: A short mobile-friendly questionnaire collects budget, savings, timeline, property type, preferred area and readiness signals such as pre-approval. Tools: Custom web form, Google Sheets. Benefit: Structured first-party data instead of a vague "contact me" message. Every lead arrives with the context needed to help them.
3. Process the questionnaire: Google Apps Script picks up each new submission, cleans the answers and runs the calculations the Blueprint needs. Tools: Google Apps Script, Google Sheets. Benefit: Consistent processing in minutes, with no copy-pasting or manual data entry. The same rules apply to every lead.
4. Generate a personalized Buyer Blueprint: The script fills a branded, pitch-deck-style template with the buyer's own numbers and next steps, then exports it as a PDF. Tools: Google Apps Script, ChatGPT, Claude, Google AI Studio. Benefit: Personalization at scale. Each buyer gets a plan that feels hand-made, and AI tools helped me write the copy and develop the script logic.
5. Categorize the lead for follow-up: Each submission gets an internal status: hot, warm, cold or needs work. The status depends on timeline, finances and readiness. Tools: Google Apps Script, Google Sheets. Benefit: Lead qualification means follow-up time goes to the people ready to act. Longer-term leads still get nurtured instead of forgotten.
6. Send communications and enable booking: The Blueprint is emailed to the buyer automatically. A booking system built into the site (not a third-party widget) checks calendar availability, sends confirmation emails and creates the meeting link, so the buyer books without leaving the page. Tools: Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Meet, Google Apps Script. Benefit: Instant value, then a frictionless next step. The buyer is never waiting on a manual reply to book.
7. Track submissions and appointments: Questionnaire submissions and bookings are logged in separate spreadsheets, so I have a simple, searchable record of the pipeline. Tools: Google Sheets. Benefit: A lightweight CRM. I can see how many leads are at each stage and follow up on time, without paying for software.

## Skills, with evidence

### SEO and search

- Google Search Console: Set up on both live sites. I used it to get the relaunched real estate site indexed, and I monitor queries and impressions.
- Local SEO and service-area pages: City guides for Mississauga, Milton and Oakville, built around first-time buyer searches.
- On-page SEO and information architecture: Descriptive titles, FAQ content and grade and price pages on Castoreum Canada.
- Bilingual (EN/FR) content structure: A French homepage for the French perfumery market.
- Keyword research: Used to plan page topics. Formal methods covered in Google course 2.

### Content and copywriting

- Conversion copywriting: Value-first headlines and CTAs, for example "Your first home starts with a plan, not a guess."
- Long-form lead magnets: A 28-page GTA First-Time Buyer Guide with a gated landing page.
- Educational and FAQ content: A buyer FAQ answering grades, legality, documents and pricing questions.
- B2B content strategy: Content that educates specialist international buyers before they inquire.
- AI-assisted content workflows: ChatGPT, Claude and Google AI Studio for drafting, with my own editing and fact-checking.

### Social media and creative

- CapCut: Short-form video editing for social.
- Meta Business Suite: Facebook and Instagram presence for my real estate brand.
- Landing-page content: City pages, a gated guide page and seller report page, each with one clear CTA.

### Websites and CRO

- Website building: Two live sites: relaunched hammadtherealtor.ca and built castoreumcanada.ca.
- Landing pages and funnels: Buyer Blueprint, seller report and guide download pages, each with one clear CTA.
- Low-friction inquiry design: Pre-written quote and WhatsApp messages for export buyers.
- Site health (SSL, maintenance): Fixed the SSL and maintenance problems on the older real estate site.

### Marketing ops and automation

- Google Apps Script: Processes the questionnaire, generates the PDFs, sends the emails and powers booking.
- Google Sheets as a lightweight CRM: Separate trackers for submissions and bookings.
- Lead scoring and qualification: Hot, warm, cold and needs-work categorization for follow-up.
- Make (no-code automation): Make Intermediate badge: HTTP requests, webhooks, error handling and functions.
- Email workflows: Automated Blueprint delivery and booking confirmations.

### Analytics and ads

- Google Analytics 4: Tracking both live sites behind a cookie consent banner. Funnel events are the next step.
- Privacy and cookie consent: Optional analytics cookies the visitor can decline.
- Google Ads and SEM: Covered in "Attract and Engage Customers with Digital Marketing" (October 2026).
